newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 2.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Congress party's plan to topple Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda hits snag over fears that right wing Bharatiya Janata Party would be real beneficiary
** Congress says it is prepared to accept another candidate from the ruling United Front alliance to replace embattled Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whom it has vowed to topple

"I am not against any member of the Steering Committee (of the United Front). My only complaint is against Deve Gowda," Congress president Sitaram Kesri says in a television interview two days after declaring himself a candidate for the top job
** Parliament officials say all major parties are locked in talks to rescue the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from the political chaos

** Hong Kong-based Star TV's news programme quotes Congress president Kesri as hinting that he will accept G.K. Moopanar, head of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) -- a key constituent of the United Front, as the next prime minister
** All eyes on TMC party meeting, scheduled for later in the day, the Business Standard newspaper reports
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram launches all-out bid to rescue the budget, Economic Times newspaper says
"I believe this is the least we parliamentarians owe to India," the newspaper quotes Chidambaram as saying in a statement
The newspaper says there is a move to convene parliament on April 10 -- a day before the deadline for Deve Gowda's confidence vote -- to approve the Finance Bill
** India and Pakistan, fresh from upbeat peace talks, say the political crisis in New Delhi might delay efforts to resume substantive bilateral negotiations
** Foreign Minister Inder Gujral postpones planned visit to the United States because of India's political crisis, state department says
Gujral was to have gone to Washington at the end of next week for talks with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright
MARKETS:
** Indian shares gain on Tuesday as domestic funds and some foreign players bid on dips during day of wild swings wrought by the political crisis, dealers say
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ends 66.12 points, or 2.0 percent, higher to close at 3427.01 on news the United Front is determined to pass the federal budget
** National exchange index gains 2.90 points to 970.15, Delhi 12.2 points to 725.48 and Madras 31.46 points to 3,370.83
** Unfolding political drama is unlikely to infect the rupee as the central bank possesses more than enough muscle to dampen any speculative fever, foreign exchange dealers say
** Foreign investors caught unawares by sudden crisis triggered during long Easter weekend, mark prices of overseas listed equity sharply lower as they returned on Tuesday, traders say
** HSBC GDR index closes 6.87 points, or 8.86 percent, lower at 70.72
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
